questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Solve : \($\left(D^2+6 D+8\right) y=e^{-2 x}\).$
questions.solution:
The characteristic equation is \(p²+6 p+8=0\)
\(\Rightarrow(\mathrm{p}+$4)(\mathrm{p}+$2)=0 \Rightarrow $\mathrm{p}=-$4 $\text{ and }-$2\)
The C.F. is \(\mathrm{Ae}^{-4 x}+\mathrm{Be}^{-2 x}$\)
Particular integral,
\$(\begin{aligned}$$\text{ P.I. }$& =\frac{1}{D^2+6 D+8}$e^{-2 x} \\
& =\frac{1}{(D+4)(D+2)}$e^{-2 x}
\end{aligned}\)
Since, \(f(D)=(D+2) q(D)\)
\(=\frac{1}{\theta(-2)} \mathrm{xe}^{-2 \mathrm{x}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{xe}^{-2 \mathrm{x}}$\)
Hence the general solution is
\(y=A e^{-4 x}+B e^{-2 x}+\frac{1}{2}$x e^{-2 x}\)

questions.q: The diffrerential equation \($\frac{d y}{d x}+\frac{1}{x} \sin$2 y=x³ \cos ^2 y\) represents a family of curves given by the equation
questions.solution:
The given equation can be converted to linear form by dividing both the sides by \(\cos ^2 \mathrm{y}\). We get
\(\sec ^2 \mathrm{y} \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}2 \tan \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{x}^3\)
Put tan \(y=z \Rightarrow \sec ^2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d z}{d x}\)
The equation becomes \(\frac{d z}{d x}+\frac{2}{x}z=x³\), which is linear in \(z\) The integrating factor is
\(\text{I.F. }=e^{\int \frac{2}{x} d x}=e^{2 \log x}=e^{\log x²}=x²\)
Hence, the solution is
\(z\left(x^2\right)=\int x^3\left(x^2\right) d x+a \Rightarrow x²=\frac{x^6}{6}+a,\)
\(a\) is constant of integration.
 \begin{aligned}& \therefore(6 $\tan y$) x²=x⁶+6 a \Rightarrow 6 x² $\tan y=x$⁶+c, \\
& \quad[c=6 a]
\end{aligned} \)

questions.q: $The solution of the differential equation \left(1+y^{2}\right)+\left(x-e^{\tan ^{-1} y}\right) \frac{d y}{d x}=0$
questions.solution: $1+y^{2}+\left(x-e^{\tan ^{-1} y}\right) \frac{d y}{d x}=0\Rightarrow\left(1+y^{2}\right) d x=\left(e^{\tan ^{-1} y}-x\right) d y\Rightarrow \frac{d x}{d y}=\frac{e^{\tan ^{-1} y}-x}{1+y^{2}}\Rightarrow \frac{d x}{d y}+\frac{1}{1+y^{2}} \cdot x=\frac{e^{\tan ^{-1} y}}{1+y^{2}}$ Which is the linear different equation of the form $\frac{d x}{d y}+R x=S$, where $R$ and $S$ are functions of $y$ or constant $(s)$ \therefore $\mathrm{I} . \mathrm{F}=\int_ e^{\int \frac{1}{1+y^{2}} \cdot$ d y}=e^{\tan ^{-1} y} Hence required solution is $\begin{array}{l}$ x .($\mathrm{I} . \mathrm{F})=\int \frac{e^{\tan ^{-1} y}}{1+y^{2}}(\mathrm{I} . \mathrm{F})$ d y \\ \Rightarrow x $\cdot$ e^{\tan ^{-1} y}=$\int \frac{e^{\tan ^{-1} y}}{1+y^{2}}\left($ e^{\tan ^{-1} y}\right) d y \\ \Rightarrow x $\cdot$ e^{\tan ^{-1} y}=$\int \frac{e^{2 \tan ^{-1} y}}{1+y^{2}}$ d y \end{array} Put $ t=\tan ^{-1} y \begin{array}{l} \therefore\frac{d t}{d y}=\frac{1}{1+y^{2}} \Rightarrow$ d t=$\frac{1}{1+y^{2}} \cdot$ d y \\ \therefore $\int \frac{e^{2 \tan ^{-1} y}}{1+y^{2}}$ d y=$\int$ e^{2 t} $\cdot$ d t=$\frac{e^{2 t}}{2}+$ K \end{array} Hence equation (1) becomes, $\begin{array}{l}$ x e^{\tan ^{-1} y}=$\frac{1}{2}$ e^{2 t}+K \\ \Rightarrow x e^{\tan ^{-1} y}=$\frac{1}{2}$ e^{2 \tan ^{-1} y}+K \\ \Rightarrow 2 x e^{\tan ^{-1} y}=e^{2 \tan ^{-1} y}+K \end{array}

questions.q: The differential equation $(3 x+4 y+1) d x+(4 x+5 y+1) d y=0$ represents a family of
questions.solution: The given differential equation is $(3 x+4 y+1) d x+(4 x+5 y+1) d y=0$ Comparing eq. (i) with $\mathrm{Mdx}+\mathrm{Ndy}=0$, we get M=3 x+4 y+1 and $\mathrm{N}=4 \mathrm{x}+5 \mathrm{y}+1$ Here, $\frac{\partial \mathrm{M}}{\partial \mathrm{y}}=\frac{\partial \mathrm{N}}{\partial \mathrm{x}}=4$ Hence, eq. (i) is exact and solution is given by $\begin{aligned} & \int(3 x+4 y+1) d x+\int(5 y+1) d y=C \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{3 x^{2}}{2}+4 x y+x+\frac{5 y^{2}}{2}+y-C=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 3 x^{2}+8 x y+2 x+5 y^{2}+2 y-2 C=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 3 x^{2}+2.4 x y+2 x+5 y^{2}+2 y+C^{\prime}=0 \\ & \text{ where, } C^{\prime}=-2 C \end{aligned}$ On comparing eq. (ii) with standard form of conic section $a x^{2}+2 h x y+b y^{2}+2 g x+2 f y+C=0$ We get, $\mathrm{a}=3, \mathrm{ h}=4, \mathrm{ b}=5$ Here, $h^{2}-a b=16-15=1 > 0$ Hence, the solution of differential equation represents family of hyperbolas.

questions.q: The solution of $\frac{d^{2} x}{d y^{2}}-x=k$, where $k$ is a non-zero constant, vanishes when $y=0$ and tends of finite limit as $y$ tends to infinity, is
questions.solution:
We can write given differential equation as,
$\left(\mathrmD^{2}-1\right) \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{k}$ ...(i)
where, $D \equiv \frac{d}{d y}$ 
Its auxiliary equation is $m^{2}-1=0$, so that $\mathrm{m}=1,-1$
Hence, $C F=C_{1} e^{y}+C_{2} e^{-y}$.
where $\mathrm{C}_{1}, \mathrm{C}_{2}$ are arbitrary constants
Now, also $\mathrm{PI}=\frac{1}{\mathrmD^{2}-1} \mathrm{k}\begin{array}{l}
=\mathrm{k} \cdot \frac{1}{\mathrmD^{2}-1} \mathrme^{0 . \mathrm{y}} \\
=K \cdot \frac{1}{0^{2}-1} e^{0 . \mathrm{y}}=-K
\end{array}
So, solution of eq. (i) is 
$x=C_{1} e^{y}+C_{2} e^{-y}-k$ ...(ii)
Given that $x=0$, when $y=0$
So, $0=$\mathrm{C}_{1}+\mathrm{C}_{2}-\mathrm{k} \quad (From (ii)) 
 ⇒ \mathrm{C}_{1}+\mathrm{C}_{2}=\mathrm{k} ...(iii)
Multiplying both sides of eq. (ii) by $\mathrme^{-$\mathrm{y}$}$, we get
x. $\mathrme^{-$\mathrm{y}$}=$\mathrm{C}_{1}+\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrme^{-2 \mathrm{y}}-\mathrm{ke}^{-\mathrm{y}} ...(iv)
Given that $x  → m$ when $y $\rightarrow \infty,$m$ being a finite quantity.
So, eq (iv) becomes
\mathrm{x} \times$0=$\mathrm{C}_{1}+\mathrm{C}_{2} \times$0-($\mathrm{k} \times$0)\Rightarrow \quad $\mathrm{C}_{1}=$0$ ...(v)
From eqs. (iv) and (v), we get \mathrm{C}_{1}=$0$ and  \mathrm{C}_{2}=\mathrm{k}
Hence, eq. (ii) becomes
\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{ke}^{-\mathrm{y}}-\mathrm{k}=\mathrm{k}\left(\mathrme^{-\mathrm{y}}-$1\right)

questions.q: $The solution of the differential equation \frac{d y}{d x}+\frac{2 y x}{1+x^{2}}=\frac{1}{\left(1+x^{2}\right)^{2}}$ is
questions.solution:
$\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}+\frac{2 \mathrm{yx}}{1+\mathrm{x}^{2}}=\frac{1}{\left(1+\mathrm{x}^{2}\right)^{2}}$
which is a linear differ ential equation.
Here, $\mathrm{P}=\frac{2 \mathrm{x}}{1+\mathrm{x}^{2}}, \mathrm{Q}=\frac{1}{\left(1+\mathrm{x}^{2}\right)^{2}}$
Now, IF = $\mathrm{e}^{\int P d x}=\int_{\mathrm{e}^{1+\mathrm{x}^{2}}}^{\int \frac{2 \mathrm{x}}{1+\mathrm{dx}}}=\mathrm{e}^{\log \left(1+\mathrm{x}^{2}\right)}=\left(1+\mathrm{x}^{2}\right)\therefore$ Solution of differential equation is

\Rightarrow y\left(1+x^{2}\right)=\int \frac{1}{1+x^{2}}d x+C \\
\Rightarrow y\left(1+x^{2}\right)=\tan ^{-1} x+C
\end{array}$

questions.q: $The solution of the differential equation \frac{d y}{d x}=(4 x+y+1)^{2}$, is
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{l}\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=(4 \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}+1)^{2}...(i) \\

questions.q: If $x=-9$ is a root of $\left|\begin{array}{lll}x & 3 & 7 \\ 2 & x & 2 \\ 7 & 6 & x\end{array}$\right|=0$, then other two roots are$
questions.solution:
Given $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x & 3 & 7 \\ 2 & x & 2 \\ 7 & 6 & x\end{array}$\right|=0$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow x \left[x^{2}-12\right]$-3[2 x-14]+7[12-7 x]=0 \\
\Rightarrow x^{3}-67 x+126=0
\end{array}$
But given $(x=9)$ is a root of given determinant.
$\therefore($\mathrm{x}+$9)$ is a factor
$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \mathrmx^{3}+9 \mathrmx^{2}-9 \mathrmx^{2}-81 $\mathrm{x}+$14 $\mathrm{x}+$126=0 \\
\Rightarrow \mathrmx^{2}($\mathrm{x}+$9)-9 $\mathrm{x}(\mathrm{x}$+$9)+14(\mathrm{x}$+$9)=0
\end{array} \Rightarrow(x+9) \left(x^{2}-9 x+14\right)$=0\Rightarrow(x+9) $\left(x^{2}-7 x-2 x+14\right)=0\Rightarrow(x+9)(x-7)(x-2)=0\Rightarrow x=-9,7,2$

questions.q: In a culture the bacteria count is $1,00,000$. The number is increased by $10 \%$ in 2 hours. In how many hours will the count reach $2,00,000$ if the rate of growth of bacteria is proportional to the number present.
questions.solution:
Let y denote the number of bacteria at any instant $\mathrm{t} \cdot$ then according to the question
$$
\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dt}} \alpha \mathrm{y} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{y}}=\mathrm{k} \mathrm{dt}......(i)
$$
$\mathrm{k}$ is the constant of proportionality, taken to be + ve on integrating (i), 
we get $\log y=k t+c......(ii)$
$\mathrm{c}$ is a parameter. let $\mathrm{y}_{0}$ be the initial number of bacteria
i.e., at $t=0$ using this in (ii), $c=\log y_{0}$
$$
\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \log y=k t+\log y_{0} \\
\Rightarrow \log \frac{y}{y_{0}}=k t......(iii)
\end{array}
$$
$\mathrm{y}=\left(\mathrm{y}_{0}+\frac{10}{100} \mathrm{y}_{0}\right)=\frac{11 \mathrm{y}_{0}}{10}$, when $\mathrm{t}=2$
So, from (iii), we get $\log \frac{\frac{11 \mathrm{y}_{0}}{10}}{\mathrm{y}_{0}}=\mathrm{k}$ (2) 
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=\frac{1}{2} \log \frac{11}{10}......(iv)$
Using (iv) in (iii) $\log \frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{y}_{0}}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\log \frac{11}{10}\right) \mathrm{t}......(v)$
let the number of bacteria become 1,00 , 000 to $2,00,000$ in $\mathrm{t}_{1}$ hours. i.e., $\mathrm{y}=2 \mathrm{y}_{0}$ when $\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{t}_{1}$ hours. from (v)
$$
\log \frac{2 \mathrm{y}_{0}}{\mathrm{y}_{0}}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\log \frac{11}{10}\right) \mathrm{t}_{1} \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}_{1}=\frac{2 \log 2}{\log \frac{11}{10}}
$$
Hence, the reqd. no. of hours $=\frac{2 \log 2}{\log \frac{11}{10}}$

questions.q: The solution of $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{x^{2}+y^{2}+1}{2 x y}$, satisfying $y(1)=0$ is given by
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{x^{2}+y^{2}+1}{2 x y} \\
\Rightarrow 2 x y d y=\left(x^{2}+1\right) d x+y^{2} d x \\
\Rightarrow \frac{x d\left(y^{2}\right)-y^{2} d x}{x^{2}}=\left(\frac{x^{2}+1}{x^{2}}\right) \cdot d x \\
\Rightarrow \int d\left(\frac{y^{2}}{x}\right)=\int\left(1+\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right) d x \\
\Rightarrow \frac{y^{2}}{x}=x-\frac{1}{x}+C \\
\Rightarrow y^{2}=\left(x^{2}-1+C x\right) \\
\text{ When } x=1, y=0 \\
\Rightarrow 0=1-1+C \\
\Rightarrow C=0
\end{array}$\therefore \quad$ The solution is $x^{2}-y^{2}=1$ i.e., hyperbola.$

\therefore \text{ I.F. }=e^{\int \frac{1}{t}d t}=e^{\log t}=t=\log |x|

solution is given by
